title: Commit -> purchase ledger movements + price history + stats-recompute trigger
goal: Turn a reviewed receipt (S-12's committable state) into real inventory: every matched/new_item line becomes a stock_movements purchase row, new_item lines get their catalog_items/item_aliases created for the first time (E-3 deliberately deferred this write to here), price_history is recorded, and item_stats gets minimal purchase bookkeeping — atomically, so a mid-commit failure never leaves a receipt half-applied to the ledger.
in_scope: Migration: a single Postgres function commit_receipt(p_receipt_id uuid, p_past_order_override boolean, p_new_item_qty_base jsonb default '{}') that does the entire write in one plpgsql function body (implicitly one transaction — any exception rolls back everything, so there is no partially-committed receipt). Re-validates purchased_at is not null and purchased_at_confirmed=true, and that zero receipt_lines for the receipt remain review_state='needs_review', raising an exception (which the Server Action surfaces as an error, no writes applied) if either fails — server-side re-check independent of S-12's client/action-level guard, same defense-in-depth posture as extension re-validation elsewhere in this repo (app/add/actions.ts).

For each receipt_line with review_state IN ('matched','new_item') (excluded rows are skipped entirely, needs_review is already guarded against above): matched lines use their existing matched_item_id/qty_base exactly as currently stored — never re-derived or re-matched inside commit (see invariants; this is the fix for the alias-ordering bug an advisor review caught in this epic's planning, see ledger). new_item lines resolve category_id + base_unit from categories by category_slug (rejecting an unresolved/'uncategorized' slug — S-12's UI already prevents confirming a new_item with 'uncategorized', this is the server-side backstop), insert one catalog_items row and one item_aliases row (source='commit', confidence=1.0), and update the receipt_line's matched_item_id + qty_base in place.

qty_base for new_item lines is computed in TypeScript before calling the function (via S-10's existing normalizeUnitToBase, target base_unit = the resolved category's default_base_unit — not re-derived ad hoc from unit_display, so the source of truth for what a category's base unit is stays exactly what S-10/categories already establish) and passed in as p_new_item_qty_base, a {line_id: qty_base} map — keeps the one piece of non-trivial conversion logic (regex-based unit parsing) in one place (lib/receipts/canonicalize.ts) instead of duplicating it in SQL.

stock_movements: one 'purchase' row per committed line at occurred_at=receipts.purchased_at. If p_past_order_override is true AND purchased_at < household.stock_epoch, ALSO write a second 'initial' row at occurred_at=now() for the same qty_base — mirrors the exact pattern lib/onboarding/data.ts's completeOnboarding already uses for 'items already at home': an 'initial' movement counts toward v_current_stock (which filters on occurred_at >= stock_epoch) without corrupting the frequency engine's purchase-interval history (E-5 only reads type='purchase' events per working spec Sec5 step 1), because it's a different movement type at a different timestamp.
price_history: one row per line where unit_price is not null (catalog_item_id, merchant=receipts.merchant, unit_price, observed_at=purchased_at).

item_stats: minimal bookkeeping only — an upsert (insert ... on conflict (catalog_item_id) do update) incrementing purchase_count and advancing last_purchased_at to the greatest of its current value and this commit's purchased_at. This is the 'stats-recompute trigger' named in the story title in the loosest sense the acceptance criterion actually requires: no EWMA, no cadence_bucket, no confidence, no daily_rate — the full algorithm (working spec Sec5) is E-5's job, not built yet, and this story does not stand it up early.
On success, receipts.status is set to 'committed'.
Server Action commitReceiptAction(receiptId, pastOrderOverride): computes new_item qty_base map, calls the RPC, revalidates the /review and /review/[id] paths.
out_of_scope: The prediction engine itself (EWMA/shrinkage/rate-cross-check/confidence/cadence bucketing, working spec Sec5) — E-5, a separate not-yet-built epic. This story's item_stats write is deliberately the smallest thing that could be called a 'stats-recompute trigger' without reimplementing E-5 early.
Repurchase reconciliation / rate_correction (F9.3) — depends on the prediction engine existing first (E-5+).

An 'uncommit' or edit-after-commit action — no acceptance criterion requires reversing a commit; receipt_lines/stock_movements stay as the audit trail (ADR-0001) if a correction is ever needed later, via a future adjustment movement, not by mutating history.

Cross-request concurrency control beyond what the single atomic function call already gives (Postgres serializes function execution per row-lock via the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the receipt row) — single-household v1, matches ADR-0004's posture of not over-building for a concern this product doesn't have yet.
acceptance: Committed receipt's items appear in inventory in correct base-unit quantities (Day 1 gate, A1).
invariants: Never re-runs matching (matchCatalogItem / find_best_alias_match) inside the commit function or the Server Action that calls it — every line's identity (matched_item_id, or 'this line creates a new catalog item') is exactly what S-12 already resolved it to before Commit was pressed. This is load-bearing: re-matching during commit would let a same-receipt earlier new_item's freshly-inserted alias trigram-match a later, genuinely different line within the same loop.

Two new_item lines on one receipt intentionally create two distinct catalog_items rows, even if their text is similar — each is a line a human looked at and explicitly confirmed as 'new item' via S-12; commit does not second-guess that decision by trying to merge them.

A commit either fully applies (status becomes 'committed', every line's movements/price_history/item_stats/catalog rows exist) or fully fails (an exception aborts the whole function, no rows from this receipt's commit attempt persist) — no partial-application state is reachable.

A backdated purchase (purchased_at < stock_epoch) without the override checkbox writes only the historical 'purchase' movement and never touches v_current_stock's visible total for that item (A18) — this requires no special-case code, since v_current_stock's own occurred_at >= stock_epoch filter already does the work; verification must positively confirm this rather than assume it.
